tentative

/TEN-uh-tiv/ — stress on first syllable · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Tentative describes something not yet fixed or certain, treated as a first attempt that could still change or fall through rather than a final decision.

They set a tentative date for the picnic, weather permitting.

Example

The startup announced a tentative product launch for June, but warned investors that the date could shift if development fell behind.

Tentative is more precise than "unsure" because it emphasizes not personal doubt but rather a provisional arrangement—a first attempt that is deliberately left open to change. This is exactly what a business announcement requires.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

provisional: Provisional describes an official stand-in: an arrangement formally adopted to serve until something final replaces it — a provisional government runs a country while elections are arranged. Tentative is looser and earlier: a first attempt, floated while things could still change or fall through. Provisional stands in; tentative tests the water.

uncertain: Uncertain describes a state of not knowing — an outcome is unsettled, or a person is unsure. Tentative describes a plan deliberately offered as a draft: the date is set, but everyone agrees it may move. Uncertain is about the doubt itself; tentative is about an arrangement left open.

hesitant: Hesitant describes a person holding back because of doubt — a hesitant speaker, a hesitant step. Only people and their actions hesitate. Tentative can describe the plan itself: a tentative schedule is not shy, just openly subject to change. Hesitant lives in someone's nerves; tentative lives in the arrangement.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

definite: fixed, settled, and not changing

resolute: firm and unwavering, without any hesitation

Where it sits · how uncertain the plan still is

confirmed → likely → doubtful → tentative

confirmed vs. tentative: Confirmed sits at the certain end of the scale, far from tentative: a confirmed plan is locked in, while a tentative one is only a provisional first attempt.

likely vs. tentative: Likely is more certain than tentative — a likely date will probably hold, but a tentative date is openly subject to change.

doubtful vs. tentative: Doubtful is less certain than tentative: a tentative plan is still expected to happen in some form, while a doubtful one may not happen at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — tent-: to try, test, touch (from tentare) (Latin)

Suffix — -ative: tending to, of the nature of (Latin)

Put it together: Tent- ('to try, test', from Latin tentare) + -ative ('of the nature of') means 'of the nature of a trial' — a tentative plan is a test run, made to be revised rather than treated as a final decision.

Use the root in a new word: attempt: Lena's first attempt at the high jump knocked the bar clean off.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / neutral

Use tentative when you're putting forward a plan, schedule, or arrangement as a first draft that is likely to change or be finalized later. Use "provisional" for official temporary arrangements. Use "uncertain" or "unsure" for personal feelings of doubt.
